session.question: How sustainability reporting link with SDGs and sustainability performance, it matter from the supply chain framework too?
session.answer:
Sustainability reporting links with the SDGs by using the 17 SDGs as an explicit reference framework for defining, disclosing, and evaluating a firm’s contribution to sustainable development. In the principle-based reporting view, firms should report outcomes and impacts against the SDGs rather than relying only on performance rankings or inter-firm comparisons. This shifts reporting from generic disclosure to evidence of substantive sustainability contribution. The framework is also intended to integrate with financial/economic reporting and with integrated thinking, so sustainability performance is treated as part of overall organizational performance. (abeysekera2022aframeworkfor chunk 1)

The supply chain framework matters because it is the practical mechanism through which sustainability and SDG alignment are implemented across supplier-to-customer activities. Evidence from SMEs indicates that sustainable supply chain practices are positively and significantly associated with financial performance, and also positively associated with SDGs; SDGs, in turn, positively affect financial performance. This implies a causal chain in which supply chain sustainability improves operational efficiency and reduces environmental and social harms, thereby strengthening sustainability performance and business results. (rismawati2024exploringtherelationship chunk 1)

More broadly, life cycle and supply chain-based assessment frameworks can connect ESG reporting to SDG-aligned sustainability performance across product and system life cycles. Such frameworks make reporting more actionable by identifying issues along the value chain and supporting targeted improvements across environmental, social, governance, and economic dimensions. (padilla‐rivera2024enhancingenvironmentalsocial chunk 1)

session.formatted_answer:
Question: How sustainability reporting link with SDGs and sustainability performance, it matter from the supply chain framework too?

Sustainability reporting links with the SDGs by using the 17 SDGs as an explicit reference framework for defining, disclosing, and evaluating a firm’s contribution to sustainable development. In the principle-based reporting view, firms should report outcomes and impacts against the SDGs rather than relying only on performance rankings or inter-firm comparisons. This shifts reporting from generic disclosure to evidence of substantive sustainability contribution. The framework is also intended to integrate with financial/economic reporting and with integrated thinking, so sustainability performance is treated as part of overall organizational performance. (abeysekera2022aframeworkfor chunk 1)

The supply chain framework matters because it is the practical mechanism through which sustainability and SDG alignment are implemented across supplier-to-customer activities. Evidence from SMEs indicates that sustainable supply chain practices are positively and significantly associated with financial performance, and also positively associated with SDGs; SDGs, in turn, positively affect financial performance. This implies a causal chain in which supply chain sustainability improves operational efficiency and reduces environmental and social harms, thereby strengthening sustainability performance and business results. (rismawati2024exploringtherelationship chunk 1)

More broadly, life cycle and supply chain-based assessment frameworks can connect ESG reporting to SDG-aligned sustainability performance across product and system life cycles. Such frameworks make reporting more actionable by identifying issues along the value chain and supporting targeted improvements across environmental, social, governance, and economic dimensions.
